instruction: Create a single-page SVG product illustration of a modern toilet with a clearly visible flush handle or button. Show the tank, lid, seat, bowl, plumbing base, and flusher in convincing proportion, with ceramic highlights and subtle shading. Include a tasteful bathroom context and a small visual cue that communicates flushing action, while keeping the toilet the clear focal object. Put strong emphasis on dimensionality, material realism, clean composition, and refined vector finish.

history.critique: The page chrome is genuinely strong (monospace technical labels, clean spec table, consistent pill system, good title hierarchy), but the illustration under-delivers on the brief's core. Brief & intent: tank, seat, bowl, and dual flusher are present, but the lid is ambiguous — the horizontal slab between tank and seat reads as a floating board, not a lid; the 'plumbing base' is a tiny chrome knob with no flange or trap; and the required 'visual cue of flushing action' is absent — the only cue is the dark FLUSH[F] pill, which is a UI control, not an in-scene cue, while the water is a static flat mint oval. Clarity & hierarchy: the projection is mixed — tank and bowl are front-facing while the seat, water, and flush buttons are drawn from directly above, so the object reads as two views welded together; the 'FRONT ELEVATION' tag contradicts this; the mint oval is ambiguous (water vs. colored seat); and the highest-contrast element in the canvas is the dark FLUSH pill, inverting the intended focal hierarchy — the pale toilet recedes while the UI advances. Craft: the ceramic is near-monochrome pale blue-gray with almost no value range — no core shadow, no crisp specular, no rim light — so 'ceramic highlights, subtle shading, and dimensionality' are not achieved; the water has no meniscus, depth, or reflection; the seat floats with no hinge or contact shadow; the base is underscaled. Expressiveness: the FIG.07 / scale / monospace technical-study framing is a good identity and the teal accent is a nice signature, but the missed flush moment and the ghostly render make the hero feel generic; the plant is good context, the wall dispenser is arbitrary. Real trade-offs: the light technical aesthetic conflicts with material realism (resolve by adding value contrast inside the ceramic, not by going photoreal); a diegetic flush cue risks clutter (resolve with a minimal swirl + a few droplets); a true front elevation would hide the buttons and water (resolve with one consistent low 3/4 tilt that satisfies both 'clearly visible flusher' and 'dimensionality').
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan, all achievable with inline SVG paths, linear/radial gradients, and feGaussianBlur — no external assets. 1) Unify the projection: redraw the toilet as one consistent low 3/4 (~15–20° top tilt) so tank top, dual-button plate, seat oval, and bowl share the same axonometric; delete the ambiguous slab, draw the tank-lid edge, seat hinge, and a seat-to-bowl contact shadow; relabel the view tag to match (e.g., '3/4 ELEVATION · 18° TILT'). 2) Build the ceramic value structure: right-side core shadow, crisp left specular streak, top rim light, and a soft floor-contact reflected light; give the water a meniscus ring, a depth gradient, and a faint seat-rim reflection so it reads as water, not a colored seat. 3) Make the flusher unmistakable: enlarge the dual-button plate slightly, add a chrome bevel, top highlight, and center divider, and keep it the brightest metallic in the scene. 4) Add the diegetic flush cue: a subtle two-stroke swirl in the water plus 2–3 small droplets (or a faint arc at the button) triggered by the FLUSH control; restyle the pill as a small outline chip in the canvas corner so the product's core shadow, not the UI, holds the darkest value. 5) Rebalance focus: scale the toilet up ~15–20%, tighten the empty tile margins, and drop the plant/dispenser contrast a step so context stays subordinate. 6) Reconcile with the spec: show a rimless inner ring, a soft-close hinge hint, and a proper floor-flange/trap silhouette at the base so the 'plumbing base' reads as plumbing, and align the selected swatch tint with the rendered ceramic.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The toilet is rendered as a semi-transparent ghost/wireframe 'study,' which directly contradicts the brief's emphasis on material realism, ceramic highlights, and subtle shading — the porcelain reads as glassy outline, not opaque vitreous ceramic. The dual-flush button exists but is small, pale, and low-contrast, failing 'clearly visible.' There is no visible flush-action cue in the illustration itself (only a FLUSH chip and a footnote promise). The lid is ambiguous: the mass between tank and seat reads as part of the tank, so tank/lid/seat parts are not cleanly distinguished. The right-side wall object (plate with teal bar) is unreadable and risks looking like a broken UI element. Clarity & Hierarchy: The washed-out toilet recedes, letting the sidebar's bold 'Ceramica No. 07' and $489 compete for primary focus; the '3/4 ELEVATION · 18° TILT' chip contradicts the straight-on drawing, undermining credibility; the short base pipe and tiny flange make the toilet appear to float above the floor; the saturated teal water is the only vivid color and pulls the eye to the bowl center rather than the whole object. Visual System & Craft: The page chrome is genuinely refined (consistent mono labels, chips, spacing, palette), but the SVG is muddy: inconsistent stroke opacities, no specular highlights, a neon-teal water that clashes with the muted cream system, a flat hard-edged plant that doesn't match the soft gradient style, a near-invisible tile grid with no perspective, and a soft shadow that fails to ground the object. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: The 'FIG. 07 / SCALE 1:8 / RENDER LIVE' technical-study framing is a strong, content-specific concept, but the execution lacks its promised precision — no dimension lines, callouts, or crisp linework — so the ghostly style reads as unfinished rather than authored, and the requested memorable moment (flush cue) is absent. Real trade-offs: the low-opacity style likely aimed to keep the toilet from dominating and to fit a 'study' mood, but it sacrifices the brief's core realism/dimensionality; context elements add life but the ambiguous wall plate costs clarity; the technical framing adds identity but currently mislabels the view and is visually unfulfilled.

(2) Add the flush cue inside the illustration: a faint idle ripple in the water plus, on FLUSH/F, a ~600ms swirl/ripple and two small motion arcs at the button — subtle enough to keep the toilet the focal object. (3) Fix context and truthfulness: relabel the chip to 'FRONT ELEVATION' (or add a true slight 3/4 tilt), replace the ambiguous right-side plate with a clearly readable wall-hung flush plate echoing the button (or remove it), mute the plant into the palette, and give the floor a subtle perspective tile grid with a horizon line. (4) Rebalance hierarchy: raise the toilet's contrast against the canvas so it wins the first glance, slightly soften the sidebar's boldness, and keep the FLUSH chip as the only in-canvas control.
